### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **47** documentable anchor(s).

**46** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fa26308bb0332152a359335be27ba1a7f18574de`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `packageId (4 routes)`
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **31** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fa26308bb0332152a359335be27ba1a7f18574de` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8d5d7088abd42e67ade8d105d2ec69d4b11ed2aa` — the merge of head `768fc0b2c1a03dba28e9dc01267aab5fab49f2f3` into base `fa26308bb0332152a359335be27ba1a7f18574de`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8d5d7088abd42e67ade8d105d2ec69d4b11ed2aa && git checkout 8d5d7088abd42e67ade8d105d2ec69d4b11ed2aa
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fa26308bb0332152a359335be27ba1a7f18574de 768fc0b2c1a03dba28e9dc01267aab5fab49f2f3 && git checkout -B drift-repro fa26308bb0332152a359335be27ba1a7f18574de && git merge --no-ff 768fc0b2c1a03dba28e9dc01267aab5fab49f2f3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fa26308bb0332152a359335be27ba1a7f18574de
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs fa26308bb0332152a359335be27ba1a7f18574de` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `81d447db8c359cfdc81b16c7d200ab2967e66371`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule.test.ts, packages/rest/src/sharing-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/sharing-rule-declared-name-conflict.test.ts + packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts (`DefineSharingRuleInput`, `ISharingRuleService.defineRule`), packages/client/src/index.ts (`shares.rules.save`, :6459–6476), packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/package.json and src/index.ts, packages/rest/package.json and src/index.ts, packages/rest/src/error-response.ts (`classifiedRefusalAnswer`), packages/rest/src/rest-hook-refusal-status-passthrough.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`buildSession` :6591–6606, hook priority :4747–4754, `previous` binding :16859), packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts (`HookContextSchema.previous` :647), packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-provenance.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/rule-hooks.ts (`bindRuleCriteriaGuard`), packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/declared-sharing-rules.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/types.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.sharing-rule-declared-mirror-retired.ts, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, docs/adr/0087, docs/adr/0112, docs/adr/0131 (at `origin/main` and the D6/D7 notes at refs/review/pr-24422 = `2261458d1`), .changeset/24421-sharing-rule-declared-name-guard.md and content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx (prose faces, read for the claims the code makes about them)

Head verified against `GET /pulls/24428` twice during the review: unchanged at `81d447db8`. Diff read as `git diff origin/main...refs/review/pr-24428` (merge-base `71fa166e9`, 5 commits, 7 files, +516/−7). Inputs: card #24421 body and both comments (claim 6257564383, os-dev-report 6258334620), ruling B′ 6257388265 verbatim, the ADR-0131 D6 note at PR #24422's head, PR #24428 body, file list, the one docs-drift comment, zero review comments, the check-runs on the head.

**Check-runs on the head (their conclusions are the gate verdicts):** 40 runs. 34 `success` (Lint & Repo Gates with all its lanes, TypeScript Type Check with all lanes, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Governed Surface Queue Guard, single-claim, closing-target, Part-of, Spec property liveness, Build Core, Build Docs, Test Core 1/6, 5/6, 6/6, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected, Auto Label, filter). 5 `skipped` (Packed-tarball smoke opt-in, Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Verify CLI, Dogfood matrix shard, Temporal Conformance). **1 still `in_progress` at the time of this record: `Test Core (3/6)`** (Test Core 2/6 and 4/6 completed `success` between my first and last poll). No run concluded `failure`. The dev's local report at this head: plugin-sharing 48 files / 1152 tests, rest 9 files / 684 tests, both typechecks exit 0, 145 of 149 derived gate commands exit 0 with the four remaining ones needing PR/event context that CI now supplies green.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff makes, read in the cited code and judged:

1. **`SharingRuleService.defineRule(input: DefineSharingRuleWrite, …)`** (sharing-rule-service.ts:193–196, :749). The parameter type gains an optional `id`. A parameter widening is non-breaking; `DefineSharingRuleWrite` reaches the published d.ts structurally through the exported class but is **not exported by name** from `src/index.ts` (the index exports `SharingRuleService` and the spec's `DefineSharingRuleInput` only). Right as a change; the unexported alias is a boundary flag (③ item 2), not a defect.

2. **`defineRule`'s accept-set narrowing** (sharing-rule-service.ts:850–859). Placed after the existing-row upsert branch, so it fires only when no stored row holds the name in the caller's scope. Then: `declaredRuleNamed(name)` — if a declaration holds the name, the write is allowed only when `input.id === declared.name` **and** `declaredRules(context, { name })` is non-empty (the projection is served in the caller's scope); otherwise `DeclaredSharingRuleNameConflictError(declared, 'create')`. Right against B′ item 2. A system context is not exempt here (pinned: `BOOT` without `id` is refused). That is safe: the repo's only non-test caller of `.defineRule(` is `packages/rest/src/sharing-routes.ts:705`; no boot or seed path calls it (the seeder retired in stage 9), so no platform write is broken by the guard.

3. **`bindDeclaredRuleNameGuard`** (sharing-rule-service.ts:247–277): `beforeInsert`/`beforeUpdate` hooks on `sys_sharing_rule`, `priority: 100` (lower runs first, engine.ts:4753 — alongside `bindRuleCriteriaGuard`'s 100 and ahead of the provenance stamp's 150), skipped for `session.isSystem`. Insert of a declared name is refused; an update is refused only when `data.name` is a string, differs from `ctx.previous.name`, and the new name is declared. `ctx.previous` is the published `HookContextSchema` contract bound on update and delete (hook.zod.ts:647; engine.ts:16859 binds it in both phases for both update shapes), and `session.isSystem` is propagated by `buildSession` (engine.ts:6606). Bound at sharing-plugin.ts:876 inside the same `registerHook && unregisterHooksByPackage` block as the criteria guard, so wherever Setup's New is guarded against match-all criteria it is guarded here too. Right.

4. **`DeclaredSharingRuleNameConflictError`** (sharing-rule-service.ts:214–230): `code: 'RESOURCE_CONFLICT'`, `status: 409`, `rule` = the vendor rule's name; the message names the rule and its object and says how to customise it. ADR-0112: `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` is a catalogued `StandardErrorCode` and `HttpStatusErrorCodeMap[409]`, so no ledger row is minted and `error.code` stays closed at both doors. Right. The class is not exported from `src/index.ts`; consumers can read the shape (`code`/`status`/`rule`), which is also what the REST arm reads. Acceptable; noted in ③.

5. **`POST /api/v1/sharing/rules` plucks `body.id`** (sharing-routes.ts:698). The route's field-by-field pluck drops unknown keys, so without this line the service could never see the edit signal; the only new accepted key is the one the ruling needs. The 409 reaches the wire through `handleError`'s classified arm (sharing-routes.ts:630–633 → `classifiedRefusalAnswer`, error-response.ts:670–683: declared status below 500 plus a string `code` → nested envelope at the declared status). Pinned at the HTTP level by the new REST test. Right.

6. **No `PATCH` or `PUT /sharing/rules` route exists** on `main` or at the head (grep of `method:` in sharing-routes.ts: GET, POST, GET/:id, DELETE/:id, POST/:id/evaluate). The card's "POST/PATCH" acceptance is met on the surface that exists; the dev measured and stated A1's falsification rather than inventing a route. Right.

7. **The trigger** (sharing-plugin.ts:470–486, :516–523): `scheduleReconcile` takes the names the write touched — the pre-image's and the written row's, each with its `organization_id` — and awaits `reconcileDeclaredRuleName` for each **before** the row's own `revokeRuleGrants`/`evaluateRule`, inside the existing `ruleRebindChain` and inside the awaited after-hook, so it completes in the write's request. Right.

8. **`reconcileDeclaredRuleName`** (sharing-rule-service.ts:1049–1059): scope is the `held` key's (`null` under `single`, the row's organization under a wall; returns early on unknown scopes or an organization outside the enumeration); if the declaration is still served in that scope → `evaluateResolvedRule(projection)`, else → `purgeGrants(ruleGrantScope(projectDeclaredRule(declared, scope)))`. `ruleGrantScope` keys declared grants by `source_id = name` plus the organization under a wall (:284–288), so a wall purge touches one organization's grants only. Right.

9. **`declaredRuleNamed`** (:1026–1029) is scope-agnostic. Consequence: in the degraded state where organization enumeration failed (`declaredScopes === null`), a declared name is refused in every organization **including the edit** (`declaredRules` returns `[]` so `editsProjection` is false). Conservative, and it matches the boot sweep's own rule for unknown scopes (hold everything). Right; noted.

**(a) The guard.**
- A create taking a declared rule's name is refused at the service (pinned for an org admin and for a system context: `{ code: 'RESOURCE_CONFLICT', status: 409, rule: DECLARED.name }`, `HttpStatusErrorCodeMap[409]`, nothing lands, grants untouched) and at `POST /api/v1/sharing/rules` (pinned: HTTP 409, `body.error.code === 'RESOURCE_CONFLICT'`, `success: false`). A rename cannot happen through the service (it upserts by name); through the `/data` door a rename onto a declared name is refused by the `beforeUpdate` hook (pinned at the hook: code + status). The refusal names the vendor rule (`rule` field, pinned; message, not regex-pinned, as the card demands). PATCH: no such route exists.
- The edit of the projected row stays open: `defineRule({ ...rule, id: DECLARED.name, active: false })` stores the organization's copy (pinned: `copy.id` is minted, not the name; `listRules` lists the copy alone; a later save without `id` upserts it). Through the `/data` door the edit is **not** available and never was after stage 9: the projection is not a row (`GET /data/sys_sharing_rule/{name}` has nothing to return) and an insert of the name is refused. So the one edit door is `POST /api/v1/sharing/rules` with `id` (and any service caller). That is "as today" on the REST surface, narrowed from "same-name POST" to "same-name POST carrying the projection's id".
- How an edit is told from a New: `input.id === declared.name`. The signal is a bare string any client can supply, so it is **intent, not proof** — a script that sends `id: name` is admitted. That is correct under B′: the write it admits is by definition "an edit of the projected declared row" (the id is the id `GET /sharing/rules` lists), the authorisation is `assertCanManageRules` as before, and the write the ruling closes — the accidental New that did not know the name was taken — is closed. Bypasses checked: `/api/v1/data/sys_sharing_rule` insert → hook refuses (non-system); `/data` update → refused only on a rename onto the name, a same-name save or a rename away passes (pinned); import → rows go through the engine's per-row `beforeInsert` under the caller's context (engine.ts:5112, the #2922 ruling) → refused; batch → per-row likewise; package install → after stage 9 nothing installs `sys_sharing_rule` rows (the repo's only insert is `defineRule`'s, :879; an unmanaged install copies definitions into the metadata ledger, not rows); system context → `/data` hook passes `isSystem` by design (ownership ceremony, migrations), while `defineRule` under a system context is still guarded.
- Not covered, and whether B′ requires it: (i) system-context `/data` writes — B′ item 2 says "Setup's New (or any write that is not an edit of the projected declared row)"; the platform's own machinery is not the write the ruling describes, the skip is documented at system-context.mdx row 40, and the sibling guards (`bindRuleCriteriaGuard` runs for everyone; the provenance stamp skips system) show both conventions coexist. Acceptable. (ii) The `/data` door's **HTTP** status for this refusal is not pinned in this PR — only the thrown shape is; it rides the generic `status` passthrough of `mapDataError` pinned by `rest-hook-refusal-status-passthrough.test.ts` (#7525). The card's HTTP-status acceptance names the service and `/sharing/rules`, which are pinned. Acceptable.

**(b) The reconcile.** The copy's creation reconciles the declaration's grants in the same request (pinned: after `afterInsert`, both organizations' declared grants are gone under `single` and `sweepOrphanedRuleGrants()` returns 0 — "before the next boot" observed). An `active` change on the copy reconciles again (pinned: a stale declared grant goes on `afterUpdate` through the `/data` door shape). Ordering is pinned with an injected failure: `evaluateRule` is never called, the declaration's grants stay, a warn is logged — so the two grant sets are never both left in force by one write. Nothing else purges or re-materialises unexpectedly: the reconcile runs only for names a declaration holds (`declaredRuleNamed` null → return), and the one addition beyond B′'s letter — the copy's **deletion** re-derives the declaration's grants at once (pinned) — restores exactly what item 1's model says returns when the overlay is dropped. The residual window the PR body admits (a record write landing between rebind and reconcile within one awaited chain) is the pre-existing #4433 shape, not widened here.

**(c) Scopes.** Under a wall the overlay is the organization's own: pinned (`org_a`'s copy revokes `org_a`'s declared grants only; `org_b` keeps its projection and grant; sweep 0). Under `single` the one overlay answers everywhere: pinned (both organizations' declared grants go). The key is the `held` key at sharing-rule-service.ts:991–998 (`name` under `single`, `name::org` under a wall) — today's holder key the ruling cites at `:887`, moved only by line drift. Both pinned.

**(d) Pins.** 13 in `sharing-rule.test.ts` (block "regime O, guarded", on the file's existing pinned engine double; `wireTrigger` binds the real plugin handler and the real service and fires the hook contexts by hand — the file's established pattern) and 3 in the new REST file. Every refusal pin asserts `code` + `status` (+ `rule`) and `HttpStatusErrorCodeMap[409]`, never a message regex; the REST pins assert the HTTP status and `error.code`, with a preservation pin (`body.id` reaches `defineRule`) and an anti-vacuity pin (an ordinary fault is still `500 RULE_DEFINE_FAILED`). Reverse-verified: three ablations reported with each leg restored (`defineRule` throw → 4 red; the trigger's reconcile call → 5 red; the `/data` hook's throw → 2 red), so each pin family has a red leg. Not re-run here (read-only).

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset.** `.changeset/24421-sharing-rule-declared-name-guard.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-sharing: minor`, `@objectstack/rest: patch`; summary `fix(plugin-sharing)!:`; `**BREAKING** (an accept-set narrowing), shipped as minor under the launch-window convention`; `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; the narrowing stated as a FROM → TO pair (`FROM 201 / 200 with the new row replacing the vendor rule, TO 409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT, naming the declared rule`) with the one-line fix (save the vendor rule back with its `id`; otherwise another name); the unchanged set and the reconcile stated beside it. This is the AGENTS.md §3 shape exactly: `(narrowing)` is BREAKING, the launch window (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, ADR-0087's 2026-09-13 level amendment) ships it `minor`, the FROM → TO pair and the fix are present, and one ADR-0087 marker is present. `Check Changeset` concluded `success`. Right. Observation, not blocking: `@objectstack/rest`'s POST door now accepts a new body key, which read alone is a widening of a published request; the lockstep `fixed` group makes the group's effective level the `minor` already graded, so nothing moves on it.

- **ADR-0087 marker — decided from the ADR's text: `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is right; do not register.** ADR-0087's ledger serves metadata upgraders — D8 (the 2026-08-30 addendum): "The ADR-0087 ledger serves metadata upgraders: `objectstack migrate meta` rewrites stored metadata", and `no-migration-prescription` "is not wrong in general … it simply cannot tell a prescription for a metadata upgrader from a prescription for a source-code consumer, and only the first is the ledger's business." D3 and the launch-window ratification owe "one D3 semantic entry per retirement family"; ADR-0131 D13 says "each retirement of an **authorable shape** is an ADR-0087 entry". This PR retires no authorable shape and moves no metadata: a stack's `sharingRules` is authored exactly as before, no spec key, export, option or stored shape changes, and the FROM → TO is an HTTP accept-set at one write door whose fix is a request key. Stage 9's entry (`18.sharing-rule-declared-mirror-retired`) was owed because it retired the seeder — D13's clause; that clause does not reach a guard. The ADR itself says what registering here would do (sixth-category table, the `registered` row): "writing one would put a prescription in the ledger that `objectstack migrate meta`, `spec-changes.json` and the upgrade guide cannot project. False data in the one ledger this whole mechanism keeps true." The dev's worry — that the gate's acceptance "rests on its prescription detector not reading this body's fix line" — is answered by reading, not by the detector: the body carries no metadata rewrite (no old-spelling → new-spelling of anything a stack author writes), so the detector's silence is a true negative, not the #8277 miss. Open question 1 → **A**. The marker's `why` text is accurate.

- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the right arm.** A write that returned 201/200 is refused 409; the PM protocol allows one arm and the narrowing dominates the subordinate widening (`id`), whose `minor` requirement the plugin-sharing grade already satisfies.

- **`Fixes #24421` is right.** Acceptance, item by item: the guard — refused through the service and through `POST /api/v1/sharing/rules`, with the vendor rule named, code and HTTP status pinned (PATCH measured non-existent); the edit path — open, pinned; the reconcile — creation and `active` change reconcile in the same request, pinned before the next boot (`sweepOrphanedRuleGrants() === 0`); scopes — both pinned; size — 523 lines (+516/−7), about half tests, against "about 0.3–0.5k"; `Clause-②` measured by the dev as a narrowing. The ADR-0131 D6 note at PR #24422's head ("Both are built by #24421 … no activation-ledger type … same-name rows are not refused as a class") describes this diff; its sentence "The row is made by editing the declared rule's projected row in Setup" is forward-looking on the Setup half (③ item 4).

### ③ Boundary flags

The report's four `open_questions`:

1. **ADR-0087 marker → A, keep `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.** Decided in ② from ADR-0087 D8, D3 and ADR-0131 D13. Recommendation B would register false data; declined.

2. **The `id` edit signal is undeclared on the spec contract and the SDK → escalate to the seat as a follow-up card (option A); not blocking this PR.** It is more than contract tidiness: `ISharingRuleService.defineRule` is typed on `DefineSharingRuleInput` (packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts:508–526, :579) with no `id`, and the SDK's `shares.rules.save` parameter type (packages/client/src/index.ts:6459–6469) has no `id` either — so a consumer typed against either published surface **cannot express the one write B′ makes the customisation door** without a cast, while the REST body accepts it. The plugin's `DefineSharingRuleWrite` and `DeclaredSharingRuleNameConflictError` are not exported from plugin-sharing's `src/index.ts`. Both surfaces are off this card's file surface and `packages/spec` is governed, so the fix is its own card: add `id?: string` ("the id of the rule this write edits — a declared rule's projection is addressed by its name") to `DefineSharingRuleInput` and to the SDK save type (a `Clause-②: yes` widening, `minor`), and export the two plugin symbols. It should land before objectui#12982 is built on the SDK, or that card uses raw REST.

3. **The delete reconcile → A, keep.** It is the same name-and-scope path, it is pinned, and it closes the mirror-image under-grant window (overlay removed → vendor rule's access back at once) that B′ item 1's model implies; it purges nothing.

4. **Setup has no edit door for a projection → A, the epic seat acts on objectui#12982.** What the server leaves: exactly one usable door. `GET /api/v1/sharing/rules` lists each served declaration as a row with `id === name` and `managed_by: 'package'` (`projectDeclaredRule`, `isDeclaredSharingRule`); `GET /api/v1/sharing/rules/{name}` returns that one projection (`getRule` :1061–1068); `POST /api/v1/sharing/rules` with `{ id: name, name, label, object, criteria, recipientType, recipientId, accessLevel, active }` stores the customised copy and answers 201; later saves upsert by name. Setup's existing Sharing Rules nav item is the generic `sys_sharing_rule` object view (sharing-plugin.ts:621), which cannot do it: projections are not rows, and `/data` insert of the name is refused 409. Therefore objectui#12982 must build its card's shape A: one list read from `GET /api/v1/sharing/rules` (no two-source merge); Edit on a row with `id === name && managed_by === 'package'` POSTs the form back **with `id` set**; Edit on a stored row saves as today; New never offers a declared name and surfaces the server's 409 (`error.code === 'RESOURCE_CONFLICT'`; the message names the vendor rule); switch-off is Edit with `active: false`. **Server gap that card will hit, for the seat:** the copy `defineRule` stores carries `managed_by: 'admin'`, `customized: false` (sharing-rule-service.ts:861–876), and `bindRuleProvenanceStamp` stamps `customized: true` only on an update of a `package`/`platform` row (sharing-rule-provenance.ts:76–78), which a projection never is. So once the copy holds the name, no server read distinguishes "customised declared rule" from "organization-authored rule" — the objectui card's "shows once, as customised" acceptance has no server answer, and that card says such a gap belongs to the server. Not in B′'s letter; a follow-up (stamp the copy at the edit door, or expose a marker on the list), not a blocker here.

The two `out_of_scope_findings`:

- **Hand-written docs.** `content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx` does not describe the guard or the id-addressed edit; the Docs Drift Check lists 29 hand-written pages naming touched anchors. The one docs edit in the diff (system-context.mdx row 40) is correct and required by `check:system-context-census`. A docs-only follow-up; release-owned pages stay untouched. Not blocking.
- **Setup's edit door.** Answered in item 4 above.

Further flags, none blocking:
- System-context `/data` writes bypass the hook by design (documented at system-context.mdx row 40); `defineRule` under a system context remains guarded.
- `declaredRuleNamed` is scope-agnostic: with organization enumeration unknown, every write of a declared name — the edit included — is refused until the next boot. Conservative and consistent with the sweep's hold rule.
- The 409 message says "save it with id" even when the caller did send the id but the projection is not served in its scope (a second organization under `single`). The message is not pinned; cosmetic.
- `@objectstack/rest` graded `patch` while its POST door accepts a new key; immaterial under the lockstep group (see ②).
